channel.title: Typography Gems
channel.description: Free typography watch: typefaces, foundries and tools.

item.title: Font Revival 0.5.0 — forty historical display faces, sources included
item.description: Forty nineteenth-century display faces (De Vinne, Bruce Fatface, ornaments and more) revived with editable masters, historical references and PDF proofs. OTF, TTF, WOFF and WOFF2. MIT or OFL 1.1, no reserved names, free; v0.5.0 of Nov 8 (53 families rebuilt, 132 tests).

item.title: DenkiChip 1.100 — a bold Japanese pixel font that now covers JIS 1
item.description: A compact 2-pixel-stroke font for short game UI copy, thumbnails and headings. Version 1.100 adds the 2,965 JIS Level 1 kanji and vertical writing. 6 px monospaced figures, 8 px kana, 10 px kanji. OFL 1.1, no reserved name; v1.000 in Feb, v1.100 on Nov 1.

item.title: Font Manager 0.9.6 — manage your fonts on Linux, no command line needed
item.description: Preview, activate or install families, build collections, and use a character map and the Google Fonts catalog on a GTK desktop. 0.9.5 adds Browse filtering and Unicode 18; 0.9.6 (Nov 5) fixes long load times and crashes. GPL-3.0, free; mature project since 2015.

item.title: Goeist Sans and Mono 0.0.2 — Geist with rounded corners
item.description: A rounded take on Geist: same proportions, spacing and OpenType features, with every corner and stroke ending softened for a warmer UI. The Mono keeps Geist Mono's coding ligatures. OFL 1.1, also as an npm package; experimental preview (v0.0.2, Nov 12).

item.title: DINDOT 0.22.0 — a rounded DIN for tables and signage
item.description: Industrial sans derived from DINish: rounded corners, circular dots and tabular figures that stay aligned in data tables. Four weights (400 to 700) with italics, as TTF and WOFF2, 949 characters. OFL 1.1; v0.22.0 from Nov 12.

item.title: Nottsu Sans JP 1.1.0 — Noto Sans JP in four colours
item.description: COLRv1 colour font based on Noto Sans JP: each glyph is painted in four colours from its centre. Variable from 100 to 900, plus nine statics; SVG table for Safari. Latin, kana and kanji, for playful headings. OFL 1.1; v1.1.0 from Nov 12.

item.title: Fontroom — try a font pairing on a real website and app
item.description: Puts a heading/body pair on a full web page and mobile app, or on your own site from its link. Hover to try, 180 curated Google Fonts or your local files, read without upload. Then gives you the setup code. MIT, free; brand new (Nov 12).

item.title: Kernest 0.8.0 — a font editor for Windows, no account needed
item.description: Glyph drawing, spacing and kerning, interpolated masters, Glyphs, UFO and designspace import, TTF, OTF, WOFF2 and variable export. Offline, installs without admin rights. Apache 2.0, free; very early preview (v0.8.0, Nov 13), installer not yet signed.

item.title: Geist Serif 1.003 — Geist's display serif, with a shape axis
item.description: High-contrast display serif with fine saw-toothed serifs, completing Geist Sans, Mono and Pixel. A variable axis changes dots and terminals: round, square, triangle, heart. OFL 1.1, added to the Google Fonts repository; released Oct 30, v1.003 on Nov 6.

item.title: CoCart Mono 1.0 beta — a mono where every figure stays aligned
item.description: Monospace in 9 weights with true italics and a variable version, all on one grid: aligned figures, distinct 0/O, 1/l/I and rn/m, box drawing and Braille for terminals, API key masking (ss02). Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Thai… OFL 1.1; beta 1 from Nov 12.

item.title: Saddha, Seela and Viriya 1.001 — three Sinhala faces by Pushpananda Ekanayake
item.description: Three Sinhala families converted to Unicode with full OpenType shaping: Saddha (text, variable 400–800), Seela (classic text) and Viriya (narrow display), with a matching Latin taken from Noto. UFO sources. OFL 1.1; v1.001 from Nov 9.

item.title: tuna-fonts 0.1.0 — a font manager for Windows, no account needed
item.description: For Windows 10 and 11: activate and deactivate without deleting, install by drag and drop with no admin rights, Google Fonts catalog, collections, compare 2 to 4 fonts, watched folders. Local, no ads. MIT, free; very young (v0.1.0, Nov 11).

item.title: Kernage — a full font editor in a single HTML file
item.description: Draw your letters, set kerning, distort them with effects, then export OTF, TTF, WOFF, variable or colour fonts. Runs offline in the browser, on desktop or phone, with no install. MIT, free; brand new (published Nov 10).

item.title: FontCraft 1.1.0 — manage, activate and identify your fonts
item.description: Font manager for Windows, macOS and Linux: library kept in your folders, on-demand activation, collections, one-click Google Fonts and Fontshare, and a local font finder that works from a picture. MIT, free; a young project (v1.1.0, Nov 10).

item.title: Font Viewer 0.2.1 — inspect a font inside VS Code
item.description: VS Code extension: opens TTF, OTF, WOFF2 and TTC, with a slider per variable axis, OpenType feature toggles, a glyph grid, Unicode coverage, the license and a ready @font-face rule. Offline. MIT; viewing is free, Pro tools $19. Young (v0.2.1).

item.title: RON 1.0.0 — ruler-straight capitals in five skins
item.description: All-caps grotesque drawn only at 0°, 45° and 90° from a bitmap grid: Black, fixed-width Mono, Dot, Scan (CRT lines) and Outline on one skeleton. 82 glyphs, no @ = % ? yet. OFL; v1.0.0 out Nov 10.

item.title: Threadline 1.0.0 — embroidered letters for games and UI
item.description: Stitched-thread family in six styles (Running, Satin, Applique, Plain, Woven, Chain): Woven for big titles, Satin and Plain stay readable at small sizes. 352 characters, Google Fonts Latin Core, TTF and WOFF2. OFL; v1.0.0 out Nov 9.

item.title: OCR-Bitcoin 2.0 — OCR-B as a fixed-width face for readouts
item.description: Monospace retraced from OCR-B for terminals and readouts: full Latin-1, all of code page 437 (box drawing, blocks, DOS pictograms), the ₿ sign and 100 Bitcoin icons. 464 glyphs, OTF, TTF and WOFF2 with SHA-256 sums. MIT; v2.0 out Nov 4.

item.title: Sixrow 1.000 — a scanline display face
item.description: Capitals drawn on six rows, with the gap between rows as a variable axis (SCAN): solid at 0, split into lines when opened. Weight, width and stair-step slant axes, plus a Mono. Full Latin Core. OFL; v1.000 out Nov 6.

item.title: Matte 0.101 — a variable sans redrawn from Inter
item.description: A variable sans from 100 to 900, started from Inter and redrawn: straight diagonals, flat-topped f and t, lower x-height. Latin with Vietnamese, Greek, Cyrillic; tabular figures, slashed zero, ss01–ss08. OFL; early (0.101, Nov 8), shapes may still change.

item.title: Dyekon 1.902 — a sans, text and mono family
item.description: Three hand-drawn families that work together: Dyekon (13 styles including condensed), Dyekon Text for reading and Dyekon Mono for code. TTF, WOFF2 and a ready fonts.css for the web. OFL; v1.902 out Nov 7, compiled fonts only, no sources.

item.title: Satare KUFIC 1.000 — square Kufic for Arabic and Persian
item.description: Square Kufic on a pixel grid: type normal text and the contextual forms and joins happen on their own. Persian letters, digits, harakat, salt and ss01–ss05 alternates. Six weights and a variable (wght). OFL; v1.000 out Nov 7.

item.title: Skrifttype 1.0.0 — activate fonts on demand on Windows
item.description: A local font manager: it catalogues your folders without moving anything, sorts serif, sans, mono, script, and activates a font for every app without installing it. Collections, comparison, glyph map. MIT, free; 1.0.0 out Nov 9, some rough edges left.

item.title: Fontarium 1.2.0 — inspect a font with F3 in Total Commander
item.description: A Lister plugin for Total Commander: press F3 on a TTF, OTF or WOFF2 to see the font, with sliders for variable axes, OpenType feature toggles, a glyph inspector and license details. It also activates fonts. Freeware, not open source; v1.2.0 out Nov 9.

item.title: Wiggle Wiggle 1.000 — a graffiti marker that wobbles
item.description: A graffiti felt-tip in Light, Regular and Bold: three alternates per glyph, rotated by calt so no two identical letters match; ss01 and ss02 hold the frames of a boil effect you can animate in CSS. Full ASCII. OFL; v1.000 out Nov 7.

item.title: Garamonto Code 1.1 — a fixed-width Garamond for code
item.description: A serif mono drawn from EB Garamond, with JetBrains Mono for symbols: Regular, Medium, Bold and italics, 150 exact-width coding ligatures, dotted zero (ss01 for a plain one), old-style figures. FontForge sources. OFL; a young project, v1.1 from Nov 3.

item.title: Monostain 1.0.0 — a code-drawn mono in the public domain
item.description: A mono inspired by JetBrains Mono, each glyph a centerline stroked by skia-pathops. Regular, Bold and italics, 383 characters (Latin Extended-A, arrows, box drawing), dotted 0 and distinct 1 l I |. Served by CDN. CC0; v1.0.0 from Nov 8.

item.title: Shalymenov Block 1.102 — compact Latin and Cyrillic headlines
item.description: A compact, angular geometric display face in Light, Regular, Bold and ExtraBold, for Latin and Cyrillic. Editable UFO masters, a reproducible fontmake build, ready WOFF2. Submitted to Google Fonts, not yet accepted. OFL with no reserved name; v1.102.

item.title: Tokenizer Mono 0.2.0 — see an LLM's tokens as you type
item.description: A COLR color font on IBM Plex Mono: its GSUB rules mimic 28 tokenizers (GPT-4o, Llama, Qwen…) and highlight each token, no JavaScript, at about 98% measured agreement. Without COLR it stays Plex Mono. Experimental; no license file in the repo.

item.title: Arris 1.015 — a chamfered sans with its own mono
item.description: An octagonal geometric sans, every corner cut at 45°, grown from a watch face's digits. Nine weights, a cursive italic, variable (wght, GRAD, WTCH) and Arris Mono for code: 105 ligatures, Powerline, Latin, Cyrillic, Greek. OFL; v1.015 out Nov 8.

item.title: fontzz — 36 variable families generated in code
item.description: 36 families drawn by a Python generator: 12 sans, 12 serifs, 9 display (Didone, Art Deco, dot matrix…) and 3 monos, each variable from 100 to 900 with 9 statics and WOFF2. Latin only, no italics or hinting yet. OFL; announced Nov 2, no version number.

item.title: Curto Serif 1.001 — a high-contrast editorial serif
item.description: A high-contrast serif for text, headlines and brand identities: roman and italic from Regular to Bold, static and variable (wght), Google Fonts Latin Core glyph set with extended Latin, punctuation and currencies. Built with gftools. OFL; v1.001 published Nov 5.

item.title: Awami Nastaliq 3.500 — Nastaliq for the languages of Pakistan
item.description: SIL's Nastaliq-style Arabic font for Urdu and South Asian minority languages, with all their diacritics and nuqtas. 3.500 adds U+088F and ₹. Caveat: it needs the Graphite engine (LibreOffice, Firefox…). OFL; out Nov 5, an OpenType version is in the works.

item.title: AZ Letter Digger 0.1 — the right words to proof a letter
item.description: A Glyphs 3 and 4 plugin that finds words to proof a letter or glyph (é, g k…) and ranks them instead of picking at random like word-o-mat, then opens them in an Edit tab. Free, MIT licence; v0.1 from Oct 24, renamed Oct 28. Requires Glyphs (paid).

item.title: Glyph Atlas 1.6 — see every alternate in a font on Mac
item.description: A native macOS app: type text and it shows every alternate, contextual substitution and ligature the font offers, with a variable axes panel and OpenType feature toggles. 1.6 filters glyphs by feature. Free, no licence stated; macOS 12+, unsigned app.

item.title: Pentas Meong Seru 1.000 — a quirky sans with small caps
item.description: A sans for posters, music headlines and websites that still works in running text: near-circular capitals beside narrow letters, true small caps, an odd K and 4. Eight weights, variable and static. Derived from Reddit Sans Condensed. OFL; v1.000 out Nov 7.

item.title: Collab Sans 1.000 — Inter with rounded terminals
item.description: A rounded neo-grotesque derived from Inter: Inter's screen legibility with semicircular stroke ends, softer for a UI or a brand. Nine weights plus italics, 2,548 glyphs (Latin Extended, Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese). OFL; v1.000 out Nov 3.

item.title: LXGW Marker Gothic KR 1.001 — the marker font goes Korean
item.description: Korean edition of LXGW Marker Gothic, a POP-style marker font derived from Tanugo: all 2,350 Hangul syllables and 4,620 Hanja of KS X 1001, plus the original's Latin. Handy for hand-lettered Korean headlines. OFL; v1.001 from Nov 5.

item.title: Typeshelf 1.0.0 — fonts that update themselves
item.description: Font manager for Windows 10/11: activation without admin rights (permanent or per session), Google Fonts and Fontshare catalogs with validated updates and rollback, variable-axis tester, duplicates, @font-face generator. GPL-3.0; v1.0.0 from Nov 6, unsigned installer.

item.title: Kern 1.1 — manage and pair your fonts on a Mac
item.description: Font manager for macOS: grid previews, per-font variable axes and OpenType features, side-by-side comparison, heading + body pairing with suggestions and PNG export, activation without touching system fonts. MIT; v1.1 from Oct 27, needs macOS 26, not notarized.

item.title: Obel Mono 1.002 — a mono that masks API keys
item.description: Monospace drawn at 12 px for reading agent code: nine weights with true italics (variable 100–900), 1,618 glyphs, box drawing and Powerline on-grid. Masked (ss01) shows secrets as dots. Coded at Typographic Systems. OFL license; v1.002, out Nov 4.

item.title: Nini Mono 1.100 — italics, Greek and Cyrillic
item.description: Nini Mono hits 1.100: five 11° italics (Thin→Bold), Vietnamese, Cyrillic and polytonic Greek, a taller x-height, box drawing and Powerline retuned to the cell. Ten TTF/WOFF2 styles. OFL license; v1.100 from Nov 5.

item.title: Satoma Sans 0.303 — a leaner geometric for the web
item.description: Geometric sans derived from Albert Sans: 9 weights with italics (18 styles). ~13% smaller WOFF2s, optional ~13 KB Latin-core CSS split, metric-matched fallback against CLS, raised t. Interactive specimen. OFL license; v0.303.0 from Nov 6.

item.title: Sausage Regular 0.100 — a fully rounded display serif
item.description: Heavy display serif with padded terminals, for menus, food packaging and vintage signage. One Regular weight, Latin (~416 glyphs), TTF. OFL 1.1 (commercial use OK); v0.100 from Just For Free Font.

item.title: Denpa Font 3.7 — maru-gothic for Japanese TV
item.description: Rounded monospace for Japanese TV subtitles, data broadcast and programme guides (JIS X 0213 + ARIB symbols). ~11,710 glyphs, derived from BIZ UD Gothic. TTF + WOFF2 (base / extended JIS). OFL license; v3.7 from Nov 2.

item.title: Wing Sans 1.003 — Chinese with readings above each character
item.description: Five OFL fonts (Noto-based) that show the reading above every hanzi: Jyutping, Yale, Pinyin (Guoyu/Putonghua) or Tâi-lô. Contextual polyphones; manual override available. Handy for learners. OFL license; v1.003 from Nov 4.

item.title: Intel One Mono 1.5 — Braille and Powerline for code
item.description: First update since the project’s return: Braille, Powerline glyphs, arrows and a round-top 3 (ss04). Four weights with italics, 1,385 glyphs, manual hinting. Designed with Frere-Jones for coding legibility. OFL license; V1.5.0 from Nov 4.

item.title: Paper Mono 1.000 — a mono for design and code
item.description: Paper’s monospace for design and code: 8 weights plus a 100–800 variable, 800 glyphs, box drawing and coding ligatures (ss01). Duospace option (ss02) for a more natural rhythm. A polished Geist Mono fork. OFL license; v1.000 from Oct 7, ~1,500 ★.

item.title: Shelf Serif 5.000 — serifs like shelves
item.description: “Shelf” slab serifs and rounded-rectangle bowls: a near-monoline serif generated in Python. Five weights (300–700) in one variable, hinted OTF/TTF, 26 KB WOFF2. Basic Latin. OFL license; v5.000 from Nov 4.

item.title: Toffee 1.000 — COLRv1 display with a long shadow
item.description: COLRv1 display font generated from code: variable weight, slant and long-shadow (SHDW) axes, four palettes. Handy for a title or a colourful UI mockup. WOFF2 + TTF. OFL license; v1.000 from Nov 4, brand-new project.

item.title: Alawonn 1.0.0 — a circular cursive display
item.description: Circular display face with a cursive feel, for headings and names. One Regular style, 378 characters (extended Latin), class kerning, npm package + CDN. OFL license; v1.0.0 from Nov 4.

item.title: fontmask 0.1.0 — mask secrets in any font
item.description: CLI tool that injects Obel Mono’s secret-masking rules into any font: secrets and tokens become dots on screen, copy-paste stays intact. Works in terminals and editors. MIT license (bundled rules OFL); v0.1.0 from Nov 5.

item.title: Saguna Mono 1.000 — a mono with a cursive italic
item.description: Rounded monospace for code with a true handwritten italic, so comments read like margin notes. Dotted 0, distinct 1lI, full-cell box drawing for tmux or htop. Four weights plus a 300–700 variable. OFL license; v1.000 from Nov 3.

item.title: Tiny5 Mono 3.000 — the 5 px pixel font goes monospaced
item.description: Monospaced Tiny5 for terminals and editors: six variable axes (weight, width, italic, roundness, bleed, jitter) for an LCD, CRT or dot-matrix look. 4,957 glyphs, Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Armenian, BDF included. OFL license; active repo (Nov 2026).

item.title: Fontcatch 0.4.0 — install fonts as soon as they download
item.description: Watches your Downloads folder, opens ZIPs and installs the fonts (variable or static, your choice), with preview, embedded license and WOFF2 export. Tauri/Rust. Free, MIT license; unsigned Windows preview, macOS build from source, Linux experimental.

item.title: t5x7 1.0 — a 5×7 pixel font for all of Europe
item.description: Small monospaced pixel font with 5×7 px glyphs covering the whole WGL4 list: Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, symbols and box drawing. Handy for a retro UI or a game. OFL license; v1.0 from Oct 31, a brand-new personal project.

item.title: Typst.otf 0.1.0 — a font that typesets math
item.description: Curiosity: a font that embeds Typst as WebAssembly and turns typed code into formulas through HarfBuzz’s experimental Wasm shaper. Works in no app without a rebuilt HarfBuzz; treat it as a demo. MPL-2.0 license; v0.1.0 from Nov 1.

item.title: Oneira 0.300 — from dream to lucid
item.description: Two-axis variable font: weight 100–900 and Lucidity, from round stroke endings (0) to sharp triangles (100). One file for soft or cutting headlines. Basic Latin and Latin-1 only. OFL license; very young (v0.300, Oct 2026).

item.title: Pollen 1.0 — Open Runde goes variable
item.description: Merges the four Open Runde weights (a rounded Inter) into one variable font: weight 400–700 and a ROND axis, from sharp to soft corners. Latin (incl. Vietnamese), Greek and Cyrillic. Great for a friendly UI. OFL license; v1.0 from Oct 31.

item.title: Kubet Mono 0.002 — a monospace drawn by code
item.description: Editor and terminal monospace generated by code: 879 characters, Cyrillic, box drawing, braille, Powerline; alternate zero and l (ss01, ss02). Free on your own machines, even for paid work; shipping it (web, app) needs written approval. Custom license; v0.002.

item.title: Miorning Goupa Hei 1.1 — a giant handwritten CJK font
item.description: Thick, deliberately clumsy handwriting for titles and posters: targets all 102,998 Unicode 17 Han characters, plus kana, Hangul, Latin and Greek. One two-face .ttc; AI-assisted, not proofed glyph by glyph. OFL license; v1.1.0 (Nov 1).

item.title: hb-subset-wasm 0.5 — HarfBuzz subsetting on the server
item.description: npm package exposing HarfBuzz subsetting as standalone WebAssembly (Cloudflare Workers, Node): keep only a page's characters, pin or narrow a variable font's axes. Moves to HarfBuzz 15. MIT license; unofficial, v0.5.0 from Nov 1.

item.title: Talha Mono 1.0 beta — a monospace with a Baroque pen
item.description: Terminal monospace derived from Monaspace Radon, its letters redrawn after writing master Figueiredo (1722). Code ligatures on by default, NF (Nerd Fonts) and Wide variants. OFL license; still in beta (beta.7, Oct 25).

item.title: fontcut 0.1 — trim a variable font for the web
item.description: Command-line tool (npx, no Python): cuts a variable font down to the axes and characters a site uses, splits it into unicode-range files and writes the @font-face. Reproducible output. MIT license; very young (v0.1.0).

item.title: FontFox 1008 — a font manager for Windows
item.description: Local manager for Windows 10/11: preview, filter and group fonts into lists, enable or disable them without restarting Adobe apps. Documentation in Chinese. Apache 2.0 license; very recent (Nov 1 release).

item.title: Protomonster 1.301 — a marker display face
item.description: Marker-style display font for headlines and short phrases, extended Latin and Cyrillic, variable from 400 to 700. Free custom license, personal and commercial use included. Recent (1.301, Oct 23).

item.title: GuanGe Kai 1.7 — the Ming court hand
item.description: Three Chinese fonts in Ming court regular script (guan-ge-ti), each drawn from a different manuscript, 20,992 characters; no Latin. Useful for classical Chinese titling. Fonts OFL, code MIT; active project (v1.7.2, Oct 30).

item.title: Galabir 4.1 — readable Glagolitic
item.description: Type in Cyrillic and the text shows in Glagolitic: angular capitals, round lowercase, ascenders borrowed from cursive. Derived from League Spartan, one Light style, TTF and WOFF2. Version 4.1 (Nov 1) adds 84 Unicode Glagolitic code points. OFL 1.1; a brand-new project.

item.title: Chrontor Variable 2.0 — in the spirit of New Alphabet
item.description: A grid-based modular face inspired by Wim Crouwel’s New Alphabet (1967): straight lines only, 45° diagonals. Version 2.0 (Oct 30) adds a variable width axis, Regular to Extended. Basic Latin, a single OTF file. Sci-fi titling. OFL 1.1; a young project.

item.title: Miracle Grove 1.300 — a soft serif drawn from Fraunces
item.description: A Fraunces derivative frozen at one optical size and softness: 4 weights with italics for headings and short text. Tabular figures, ligatures, alternates, TTF and WOFF2 with ready CSS. Version 1.300 (Oct 29) refines spacing. OFL 1.1; a young project.

item.title: Stem 7 1.001 — a pixel font that never blurs
item.description: A pixel font on a 7×7 grid, crisp with no grey pixels at 16, 32, 48, 72 and 120 px. Regular, hand-drawn Bold and variable Grid; 120 glyphs, tabular figures, WOFF2 of about 3.4 KB, npm or CDN. Glyphs as text, Python build. OFL 1.1, no reserved name; a young project.

item.title: vtt-transfer 0.2.4 — carrying VTT hinting over
item.description: Command-line tool (Python 3.11+): carries VTT hinting sources from an old version of a TrueType font, static or variable, to the new one, with an HTML report of glyphs to re-hint. Install with uv or pipx. MIT; a recent project, v0.2.4 on Nov 1.

item.title: Punctum Moderne 2.500 — a dot-matrix Didone
item.description: A dot-matrix Didone, roman and italic: each dot stands for pen pressure. Three axes, 54 named styles, 18 statics, 2 woff2 files. Version 2.500 (Oct 31) grows to 354 characters and 43 languages. OFL 1.1; a young, very active project.

item.title: Garamond Mono 1.101
item.description: An old-style serif monospace drawn from EB Garamond: Regular, Medium and Bold, each with an italic. For a terminal or code blocks with a bookish feel. OTF, TTF, WOFF2. OFL; v1.101 released Oct 18, maintained since 2024.

item.title: Balambika Sans 1.000 — Devanagari, IAST and Cyrillic
item.description: The sans companion to Balambika: Noto Sans Devanagari (Vedic accents) and Source Sans 3 (Latin, full IAST, Bulgarian Cyrillic) merged into one file per style. 6 weights with italics. OFL; first version released Oct 30.

item.title: Teletext Decoder 1.5
item.description: A teletext pixel font, inspired by the ETSI documents and decoder ROMs from the late 1980s. Handy for a retro UI or a mosaic info screen. Version 1.5 (Oct 30) adds Cyrillic and moves to OFL 1.1. TTF, FontForge source.

item.title: foton 0.1.4 — a font package manager for Windows
item.description: Installs, updates, activates and deactivates fonts on Windows without admin rights, from a registry or your own TOML manifests. Install via winget or cargo. MIT or Apache 2.0; a young Rust project, v0.1.4 released Oct 23.

item.title: Tünel 1.100 — a variable dot-matrix face
item.description: A dot-matrix face for LED signs, named after Istanbul's Tünel. Two axes: wght (dot size) and ROND (square to round dot), the grid never changes. 372 characters, Latin Core. TTF, OTF, WOFF2. OFL 1.1; v1.100 released 18 October.

item.title: On Top 1.001
item.description: Wide, very heavy capitals drawn in code from a logo. Latin Core, checked kerning and four stylistic sets (round A, long-leg R, square S and E). For headlines that hit hard. OFL 1.1; brand new, v1.001 released 18 October.

item.title: Digitype — digitize a typewriter
item.description: Turns scans of typewriter samples, even dirty or skewed, into an installable monospaced font: box a line, type what it says, and it averages every impression and traces it. Python locally or in the browser. No license stated; project started 22 October.

item.title: Forest Weathered 0.100 — Lao, Thai, Khmer and Latin
item.description: A display face drawn from a hand-painted sign in Laos, with Latin, Lao, Thai and Khmer in one file: rare for a multilingual Southeast Asian visual. OFL 1.1; beta, several letters still drafts to be redrawn before 1.0.

item.title: Valera Sans 0.6.4 — Cyrillic handwriting
item.description: Handwriting font by artist Valery Isachenkov, Cyrillic and Latin, three weights (Light, Regular, Semibold) in TTF, OTF and WOFF2. Good for captions and posters. Free, commercial use included, with credit and no font changes (custom license); v0.6.4, Oct 22.

item.title: Crooli Sans — a friendlier Geist
item.description: A Geist fork: single-storey a, round dots, simpler R and G, with no redrawing or spacing changes. Variable wght 100 to 900 with italics, Latin, Vietnamese and Cyrillic. A good UI pick. OFL 1.1; brand-new project, published 28 October.

item.title: Qu Black 1.3.0
item.description: Bilingual Chinese-Latin family for code: Mono on a strict 2:1 grid (one hanzi = two ASCII cells), proportional Sans for UI and web, static and variable files. Fonts under OFL 1.1; version 1.3.0 from 24 October, a young project.

item.title: The Mother of All Fonts 4.3
item.description: Fonts traced from the title cards of Engelbart’s 1968 demo: AllCaps, SmallCaps and Humanist, proportional, Mono for terminals and a Text cut for small sizes, plus 237 emoji. No Greek or Cyrillic. OFL 1.1; version 4.3, 25 October.

item.title: BRANDSWOT Modular 2.100
item.description: Pixel display face on a 5 × 7 grid where every pixel is laid in brickwork; weight changes the mortar, not the shape. 7 weights, italics, variable wght 300 to 900, extended Latin, CDN and npm. OFL 1.1; v2.100 from 27 October.

item.title: Carry 1.1.0 — a font that does arithmetic
item.description: Type 128+256= and the font draws 384: addition, subtraction, multiplication and integer division, with no code, only OpenType substitutions (calt). A striking demo of what fonts can do. MIT license; v1.1.0 from 25 October.

item.title: Medeo — Sans, Mono and Pixel
item.description: Latin and Cyrillic family by DNF: variable Sans (weight 100 to 900, opsz axis 14 to 32 for text and headings), Mono for code, Pixel in five dot shapes. Italics, static fonts, npm package. OFL 1.1; release candidate RC4, published 27 October.

item.title: CADR Mono 1.1.0
item.description: Terminal monospace generated in Common Lisp, with no drawing tool: 935 glyphs, Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, box drawing, braille and Powerline computed from the cell. A lighter Dark grade for dark backgrounds, same metrics. OFL 1.1; young project, v1.1.0 from 15 October.

item.title: Static to Variable 0.6.2
item.description: Command-line tool that turns a folder of static weights into a single variable font: init, build, then release as TTF and WOFF2, plus split to go back. Needs Node, Python and uv. MIT license; v0.6.2, young but active project.

item.title: Limn Sans 1.002
item.description: Rounded sans derived from Quicksand, with pin-shaped dots, nine static weights from Thin to Black, ready-made WOFF2 and CSS for the web, and alternates (ss01, slashed zero). English and symbols only. OFL 1.1; stable release published 22 October.

item.title: Sleet Mono 1.00
item.description: Hand-drawn, Comic-style coding monospace, reworked from Comic Shanns using JetBrains Mono's metrics as a reference. Nerd Font build, Homebrew cask. MIT license; very young: one style and 103 glyphs, public roadmap.

item.title: BRND ProType 1.1
item.description: Venezuelan neo-grotesque superfamily: 49 styles across Condensed, Normal, Extended and Mono, 7 weights, italics, and 3 variable fonts (weight 300 to 900, width 88 to 114.5). Version 1.1 adds ProDigit (LCD) and ProLed (5×7 dot matrix). OFL 1.1, released 25 October.

item.title: ZFontManager 0.8.1 — font manager
item.description: Tauri/Rust font manager for Linux, Windows and macOS: live previews, one-click activate and deactivate, tags, collections, side-by-side compare, specimen sheets, built-in Google Fonts browser. Everything stays local. GPL-3.0, a young project (v0.8.1 on 26 Oct).

item.title: Counterpunch — browser-based font editor
item.description: Editor for variable and complex-script fonts, no install needed: live compilation with HarfBuzz shaping, bidirectional text, in-place component editing. Opens Glyphs, UFO, Designspace, VFJ and SFD. GPL-3.0, free (paid AI add-on). Alpha: near-daily preview builds.

item.title: bited 0.3.0 — bitmap font editor
item.description: Pixel font editor (monochrome Unicode BDF) built with Godot: composable drawing tools, preview with test-text presets, generators, light and dark modes. Version 0.3.0 moves the bitmap core to Rust and reworks the preview. MIT, under active development since 2024.

item.title: Kibernetyk Mono 1.0.1
item.description: Geometric monospace inspired by the Ukrainian Cybernetics School: 7 weights, Latin and Cyrillic, and since 1.0 the 128 box-drawing characters plus block elements, handy in terminals and TUIs. OFL 1.1, a young project (v1.0 on 18 October).

item.title: Shift 0.1.1 — éditeur de fontes multiplateforme
item.description: Font editor in Rust and TypeScript for macOS, Windows and Linux: outline drawing, variable fonts (axes, sources, instances), components, UFO, Designspace and Glyphs import, variable TrueType export. Kerning is planned. Apache 2.0, first alpha: work on copies.

item.title: FontYar 1.0 — gestionnaire de fontes local
item.description: Offline Tauri/Rust font manager (Windows, Linux, macOS): scans folders of TTF, OTF and WOFF2, flags duplicates, previews your own text, live weight slider for variable fonts, exports @font-face CSS or a ZIP. Interface built with Persian in mind. MIT, brand-new v1.0.

item.title: C64 Keyboard 1.112
item.description: Display font rebuilt from photos of Commodore 64 keycaps: capitals, f1 to f12 key labels and all 63 PETSCII graphics, with an online tester. Ideal for retro-computing visuals. Public domain (CC0), TTF, OTF and WOFF2, an October 2026 project.
